prompts.prompt: We are moving from requirements to architecture. Using requirements-planning/outputs/requirements-final.md and requirements-planning/outputs/user-stories.md, prepare the inputs the architect needs for the system design interview. Write them as markdown files in handoff/. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill defines three specific files with required sections (business context, requirements summary, architecturally significant stories with architecture implications), and requires keeping every quantified metric and the demo vs production split. Without it, a model usually writes one summary file, rounds off numbers, or invents content for sections the source does not cover.

floor_checks.check: test -s handoff/business-context.md && test -s handoff/requirements-summary.md && test -s handoff/user-stories-extract.md

floor_checks.text: Strips the press release and testimonial

rubric.pass: All of: 11 min to under 3 min, 14% capacity loss, 10% recovery, 90% self-serve, p95 < 500 ms, 99.9% clinic hours, 10 min offline, 6-year audit, eu-central-1, TLS 1.2 + KMS CMK, 2027-03-01
rubric.partial: Most kept, one to three dropped or made vague

rubric.criterion: Uses the skill's three-file structure and sections
rubric.pass: business-context has deployment model and timeline; requirements-summary has functional, NFR (performance, scale, availability), security, constraints and integration sections; user-stories-extract has an Architecture Implications section covering data model, API, security and performance
rubric.partial: Three files but several required sections missing
rubric.fail: Fewer than three files, or one undifferentiated dump

rubric.criterion: Scale and scope are clear for the architect
rubric.pass: Pilot (3 clinics, 200 concurrent, 2,000/day) and production (400, 5,000, 250,000/day) kept separate; phase-1 exclusions (eligibility, payments) recorded as architecture simplifications
rubric.partial: Scale present but merged, or exclusions missing

rubric.pass: Sections the source does not cover (e.g. competitive differentiation, monitoring requirements, uptime outside clinic hours) are marked not specified or turned into questions, not filled with made-up content
Raises at least two real ones, e.g. 10-min offline drafts vs 'no PHI cached after submit', region choice for audit/SMS under EU residency, stories 1.6/1.7/2.2 lacking acceptance criteria

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Could an architect run a design interview from these files alone?

prompts.prompt: From requirements-planning/outputs/user-stories.md, write handoff/user-stories-extract.md with only the stories that drive architecture decisions, grouped by epic, each with its technical implications. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill says to keep 3-5 architecturally significant stories per epic with their technical acceptance criteria and to close with an Architecture Implications section split into data model, API, security, and performance. Without it, a model tends to keep every story or drop the implications summary.

rubric.pass: 3-5 per epic, including offline draft (1.4), consent PDF to FHIR (1.5), live queue (2.1), EHR push (2.3), SAML (2.4), PHI audit (2.5); cosmetic 2.6 and 2.7 dropped
rubric.partial: Right stories mostly, but count outside 3-5 per epic or one key story missing
rubric.fail: Keeps nearly all stories or drops key ones

rubric.pass: Each kept story lists concrete implications, e.g. real-time push for 40 screens per clinic, idempotent sync for offline drafts, immutable 6-year audit store with query by patient/staff
rubric.fail: Restates the story with no implications

rubric.criterion: Architecture Implications section in the skill's four parts
rubric.pass: Separate data model, API, security, and performance subsections synthesized across stories
Stories without AC are noted as such rather than given made-up numbers

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?

prompts.prompt: Write handoff/business-context.md for the architect from requirements-planning/outputs/requirements-final.md: the business context behind the system, nothing about implementation. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's business-context template asks for target users with scale, quantified objectives, success metrics, deployment model, differentiation, and timeline, with marketing removed. Without it, a model often summarizes the press release tone, omits the deployment model (a business constraint here), or invents differentiators.

floor_checks.text: File exists with the launch date

rubric.pass: 11 min to under 3 min, 14% capacity lost, 10% recovered within 6 months, 90% self-serve, plus pilot vs production scale
Product overview, problem, target users (buyer, staff, patients) with scale, objectives, success metrics, deployment model (customer's own AWS account via CDK, no servers to manage), and timeline
No implementation design; competitive differentiation marked not stated in the source (or limited to what the source supports) rather than invented
rubric.partial: Some implementation detail or one invented claim

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
